subject: social
title: Getting Around, Then and Now
about: How getting around and sending messages changed over time: horse and wagon to car, letter to phone and video call, candle to light bulb, washboard to washing machine, and which came first. NC 1.H.1.1: how people's inventions and achievements changed life in communities over time.
tip: Ask him which came first, then ask what people did before that invention.

cards.q: Which came first: the horse and wagon or the car?
cards.note: Long before cars, horses pulled wagons down dirt roads.

cards.q: Which came first: the candle or the light bulb?
cards.note: People lit candles at night for hundreds of years before light bulbs.

cards.q: Which came first: the washboard or the washing machine?
cards.note: People rubbed wet clothes up and down a bumpy washboard to get them clean.

cards.q: Which came first: a letter in the mail or a video call?
cards.note: People mailed letters long before phones or computers were invented.

cards.q: Which came first: the bicycle or the car?
cards.note: The first bicycles came before the first cars.

cards.q: Which is older: the radio or the television?
cards.note: Families sat around the radio to hear stories before there was TV.

cards.q: Which is older: the telephone or the computer?
cards.note: The telephone was invented long before the first computers.

cards.q: Horse and wagon, train, car, airplane. Which one came last?
cards.note: The first airplane flew in 1903, after trains and the first cars.

cards.q: Long ago, before engines, what pushed big ships across the ocean?
cards.note: Big sails caught the wind and pushed the ship along.

cards.q: Long ago, roads were bumpy dirt. What are most roads made of today?
cards.note: Pavement is the hard, smooth surface cars drive on.

cards.q: With no cars or buses long ago, how did most people make short trips?
cards.note: People walked, or rode a horse if they had one.

cards.q: Which is faster for a long trip: a horse and wagon or a car?
cards.note: A trip that took days by wagon takes hours by car.

cards.q: Today, how can you see Grandma's face and talk to her when she lives far away?
cards.note: A video call lets you see someone's face while you talk.

cards.q: Which gets a message to a friend faster: a letter or a phone call?
cards.note: A phone call gets there in seconds. A letter takes days.

cards.q: Long ago people used wagons. Today we use cars. What do both of them do?
cards.note: The tools change, but people still need to get from place to place.

cards.q: Long ago, before mail trucks, what did mail riders ride to carry letters?
cards.note: Riders on fast horses carried mail bags from town to town.

cards.q: People once typed letters on a typewriter. What do many people type on today?
cards.note: A typewriter printed each letter on paper as you pressed the keys.
